explanation: Sodium carbonate reacts briskly with dilute hydrochloric acid to release carbon dioxide gas, water and sodium chloride — one of the two test tubes NCERT uses to show that metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids the same way.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Colourless dilute hydrochloric acid, with white sodium carbonate added.
beaker_view.observation: Adding the acid sets off a brisk fizz of carbon dioxide gas, which turns lime water milky when tested.
